properties.name: MEASURED 2026-10-02: the proposed dependency-currency requirement contradicts a standing AGENTS.md rule it never names, "Do not bump the rocksdb pin as housekeeping", and none of rocksdb 0.25's leak fixes touches an API reflow2 calls. So under the rule as written the 0.25 bump is housekeeping, and only accepting the requirement and rewriting the rule would carry it
properties.source: reflow2 origin/main 491a5c9: AGENTS.md:638-647, crates/reflow2-core/src/foundation/store/backend.rs; rocksdb-0.25.0 CHANGELOG.md and src/ diffed against rocksdb-0.24.0
properties.statement:
FOUND while preparing the approved-queue item 2(c), the same-crate rocksdb 0.24 → 0.25 bump, in the dev_reflow2 hub session of 2026-10-02 (overnight, under limited autonomy).

THE RULE, reflow2 AGENTS.md:638-647 on origin/main 491a5c9 (v0.77.0): "Do not bump the `rocksdb` pin as housekeeping. … moving `rocksdb` forces a full `librocksdb-sys` C++ rebuild (~10 min) on every machine that pulls — yours, your collaborators', and every consumer project. Bump it only when a reflow2 change actually needs something the new version provides, and say which capability in the commit message. 'Latest is probably better' is not a reason." The same paragraph still calls `rocksdb` "the historically-unmaintained wrapper", the premise fact:the-unmaintained-premise-under-the-rocksdb-switch-has-moved says has moved.

THE REQUIREMENT, still `proposed`: "a new major (or new 0.x series) is adopted by its own PR … 'Adapting is work' is never a reason to stay behind." It names three legitimate hold-back reasons (an upstream regression, a deliberate protocol revision, a platform pin). The consumer recompile cost the AGENTS.md rule rests on is not among them, and the rule is not mentioned. No design node holds the rule: search_design for its words finds only rule:never-a-bare-cargo-clean-on-the-dev-box and the audit facts.

WHAT 0.25 PROVIDES, read against what reflow2 calls. The crate is rocksdb 0.25.0 (2026-08-16), engine RocksDB 10.4.2 → 11.8.1, rust-version 1.88. Its changelog has no breaking API change. Its fixes are memory leaks in:
- Options::set_info_log;
- column-family metadata, column-family creation (the create_cf error path), and the memory-usage APIs;
- option error paths and compaction filters.
reflow2-core calls rocksdb from ONE file, crates/reflow2-core/src/foundation/store/backend.rs. That file uses DB::open_cf_descriptors with create_missing_column_families, cf_handle, iterators, WriteBatch, an LRU cache, a WriteBufferManager and BlockBasedOptions. It calls none of the APIs those fixes touch. Diffing the 0.24.0 and 0.25.0 sources, open_cf_descriptors_internal and open_raw are unchanged.

SO: under the rule as written, the bump is housekeeping, and the rule says do not. Under the requirement, if accepted, the bump is owed. It is Anthony's to settle: accepting the requirement means rewriting that AGENTS.md paragraph (its cost argument answered or accepted, its "unmaintained" sentence corrected) in the same change.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether existing stores open unchanged under RocksDB 11.8.1, and whether 0.77.0 can open a store the new engine wrote (rollback). Those are measurements, not readings.
